title: Particle Model and Density
seo_title: Year 10 Science: Particle Model and Density Worksheets (GCSE Combined Science)
standard_code: KS4 Physics: Particle model of matter
standard_text: Density of materials (ρ = m ÷ V) and the particle model; changes of state and conservation of mass; internal energy; temperature changes in a system and specific heat capacity; changes of heat and specific latent heat; particle motion in gases and gas pressure.
meta_desc: Free Year 10 GCSE Combined Science worksheets on the particle model: density and its measurement, solids, liquids and gases, changes of state, internal energy, specific latent heat and gas pressure. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: During a change of state the temperature stays the same; E = mL.
body_html:
How to think about it

The particle model explains density, changes of state and gas pressure.

  • ρ = m ÷ V. Measure an irregular object's volume by displacement of water.
  • During melting or boiling the temperature stays the same: energy breaks bonds (latent heat). E = mL.
  • Gas particles collide with container walls; hotter gas means faster particles and higher pressure.
Example

54 g, 20 cm³. Density?

54 ÷ 20

Answer: 2.7 g/cm³

Example

0.5 kg ice melting (L = 334,000 J/kg)?

0.5 × 334,000

Answer: 167,000 J

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the temperature rises while a solid melts.
  • Thinking particles get bigger when heated.
  • Writing density = volume ÷ mass.

faq.q: How do you find the density of an irregular object?
faq.a: Measure its mass on a balance and its volume by the rise in water level in a measuring cylinder, then divide mass by volume.
The energy needed to change the state of 1 kg of a substance without changing its temperature. E = m × L.

faq.q: Why does gas pressure rise when a gas is heated?
faq.a: The particles move faster, so they collide with the walls more often and with more force.
